# Changelog

## v2.13.0

- ADD Firewall Manager 0.8.0 rozšiřuje `UFW pravidla` na malou bezpečnou konzoli. Číslo pravidla zachovává guarded Delete, `add p ...` přidává ALLOW port s volitelným source/destination/proto a `add srv <profile>` přidává existující UFW application profile. Přesný UFW příkaz se vždy zobrazí před potvrzením; před mutací proběhne `ufw --dry-run` a po ní read-back číslovaného seznamu.
- ADD read-only namespace: `:help`, `:srv` (`ufw app list`), `:info <profile>` (`ufw app info <profile>`), `:ver`, `:list` a `:list p <port|profile>`. Profil s mezerami je podporován jako celý zbytek příkazu.
- DIAG `:list p` spojuje skutečné listenery z `ss`, nativní UFW numbered rules a live IPv4/IPv6 filter pravidla z `iptables-save` / `ip6tables-save`; při názvu UFW profilu nejdřív načte `ufw app info` a rozpozná jeho TCP/UDP porty/rozsahy.
- SAFETY `:` příkazy jsou striktně read-only; native Edit se nezavádí. Přidávání je pouze ALLOW a používá argumentové pole bez shellu. Standardní dlouhodobá policy zůstává v `firewall.json`; nativní konzole slouží pro rychlou host-level UFW správu, profily a diagnostiku.

## v2.12.0

replacements.old: Status: **guarded manual UFW Apply implemented and cross-session ACK physically verified on dev-vm** as SysApps 2.12.0 / Firewall Manager 0.7.0 (2026-11-13). Hub/hourly auto-apply and production/new21 takeover remain disabled. Activation of an inactive UFW always requires one-time `sys_apps ufw <token>` acknowledgement from a different SSH transport; active Apply requires it only when changed managed rules can affect the current SSH management tuple, otherwise the pre-armed rollback is cancelled immediately after successful verification. Native/legacy UFW rules can be listed through `ufw status numbered` and explicitly deleted; an SSH-relevant permissive delete uses the same token+rollback protection. Add/Edit remains exclusively owned by local `firewall.json`.
replacements.new: Status: **guarded manual UFW Apply implemented and cross-session ACK physically verified on dev-vm** as SysApps 2.13.0 / Firewall Manager 0.8.0 (2026-11-13). Hub/hourly auto-apply and production/new21 takeover remain disabled. Activation of an inactive UFW always requires one-time `sys_apps ufw <token>` acknowledgement from a different SSH transport; active Apply requires it only when changed managed rules can affect the current SSH management tuple. The native UFW console lists/deletes numbered rules, supports explicit confirmed ALLOW additions by port or existing `ufw app` profile, and exposes read-only `:srv`, `:info`, `:ver` and port/profile diagnostics. Native Edit is intentionally absent; durable managed policy remains owned by local `firewall.json`.

replacements.old: - Native UFW rule cleanup is intentionally delete-only: list rules through `ufw status numbered`, never add/edit them from this path, and re-read the complete numbered snapshot immediately before `ufw --force delete <number>`. Any change in numbering/content must fail closed; after delete re-read and verify the expected remaining rule texts. Every native delete is wrapped in an independent backup/rollback of `user.rules` and `user6.rules`; deleting a permissive inbound rule that may cover the current SSH management port additionally requires the same fresh-SSH token before rollback cancellation.
replacements.new:
- Native UFW console owns lightweight host-level UFW operations only. Numbered Delete keeps the stable-snapshot + backup/rollback contract and SSH-relevant permissive deletes require fresh-SSH ACK. Add is allowed only as explicit `ALLOW` by one port or an existing `ufw app` profile; show the exact argument-vector-derived command, require confirmation, run UFW dry-run first, then verify numbered-rule read-back. Do not add native Edit or arbitrary raw UFW command execution; durable managed policy remains in `firewall.json`.
- Native console commands prefixed with `:` are read-only. `:srv` maps to `ufw app list`, `:info <profile>` to `ufw app info <profile>`, and `:list p <port|profile>` may inspect `ss`, numbered UFW rules and live iptables/ip6tables filter rules. Never shell-evaluate console input; parse to validated argument arrays.
